item.research_question: Can nanodomained nickel unite nanocrystal strength with coarse-grain ductility?
item.processing_route: Pulsed electrodeposition with a grain refiner
item.test_conditions: Quasi-static uniaxial tensile tests at a strain rate of 5 × 10−4 s−1 at room temperature
key_findings: The nanodomained Ni achieves a yield strength approaching 1.3 GPa
The material exhibits a uniform elongation as large as ~30%
The nanoscale domains effectively block dislocations and provide dislocation sources and trapping sites
The nanodomains occupy only ~2.4% of the total volume
The average domain diameter is ~7 nm
item.mechanism: The nanoscale domains act as strong obstacles to dislocation movements, and their boundaries provide dislocation sources and trapping sites, leading to enhanced strain hardening
item.limitations: The stability of the nanodomains during long-time sample storage and deformation is not fully understood
item.future_work: Further research is needed to explore the potential of this strategy for other metals and alloys
quotes: the nanodomains would elevate the strength to GPa level
the extraordinary product of strength and ductility sets the nanodomained Ni apart from all previous attempts

records.text: Paper card. Question: Can nanodomained nickel unite nanocrystal strength with coarse-grain ductility?. System: Nickel (Ni) with nanoscale domains. Processing: Pulsed electrodeposition with a grain refiner. Test conditions: Quasi-static uniaxial tensile tests at a strain rate of 5 × 10−4 s−1 at room temperature. Findings: The nanodomained Ni achieves a yield strength approaching 1.3 GPa; The material exhibits a uniform elongation as large as ~30%; The nanoscale domains effectively block dislocations and provide dislocation sources and trapping sites; The nanodomains occupy only ~2.4% of the total volume; The average domain diameter is ~7 nm. Mechanism: The nanoscale domains act as strong obstacles to dislocation movements, and their boundaries provide dislocation sources and trapping sites, leading to enhanced strain hardening. Limitations: The stability of the nanodomains during long-time sample storage and deformation is not fully understood. Future work: Further research is needed to explore the potential of this strategy for other metals and alloys. Quote: "the nanodomains would elevate the strength to GPa level"
